submission.justification: Algorithm-L3 with a threshold of 29.5 GeV is recommended as it achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.029% while meeting all constraints. This represents a significant 18.2% efficiency improvement over Algorithm-L1 (74.73% at 40 GeV) and 7.4% improvement over Algorithm-L2 (85.579% at 40 GeV). The threshold was optimized through detailed scanning around the initial best value of 30 GeV, identifying 29.5 GeV as the peak efficiency point. All three candidate algorithms meet the strict 4.0 μs latency constraint on the Level-1 FPGA hardware, and the threshold falls well within the required 20-60 GeV range. Algorithm-L3 delivers the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate, fully satisfying the primary goal.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 achieves 93.029% signal efficiency at 29.5 GeV threshold, which is the highest among all evaluated configurations. This is 7.4% higher than Algorithm-L2 (85.579%) and 18.2% higher than Algorithm-L1 (74.73%).

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 is one of the three candidate algorithms (Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, Algorithm-L3) specified in the project documentation.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 μs
requirements.evidence: All three algorithms including Algorithm-L3 meet the latency constraint. The evaluation confirmed L3_meets_latency = 1, and algorithms_meeting_latency_constraint = 3.
The recommended threshold of 29.5 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.
